Formulation
Brian presents with a two-month history of low mood, fatigue, reduced motivation, difficulty sleeping, decreased appetite, decreased sex drive, and difficulty concentrating, starting shortly after beginning a new job. He has a previous medical history of hypothyroidism and is taking Thyroxine. Significant family history includes paternal suicide. No current suicidal ideation or intent. Predisposing factors include family history and hypothyroidism; precipitating factor appears to be stress related to new employment. Perpetuating factors: ongoing fatigue and poor sleep. Protective factors: stable relationship, help-seeking behavior, current lack of suicidal ideation.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: 
- Patient Goal(s): Return to previous state of wellbeing and daily functioning
- Clinical Goal(s): Improve mood and energy; clarify possible depressive disorder versus hypothyroid contribution; address sleep/appetite concerns; screen for medical contributors
- Actions (Patient): Attend GP appointment for in-person assessment and blood tests; monitor symptoms; report any mood changes or new symptoms
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Arrange prompt in-person review and physical examination; order blood tests (including thyroid function, full blood count, other relevant investigations); assess for depressive disorder and other medical causes; provide ongoing support and follow-up

Secondary Problem:
- Patient Goal(s): Not specifically stated
- Clinical Goal(s): Address difficulties with sleep, appetite, and concentration; evaluate for impact on relationships and occupational functioning
- Actions (Patient): Engage in recommended assessments; consider sleep hygiene strategies; communicate any further concerns at follow-up
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Evaluate contributing factors to sleep and appetite disturbance; consider referral to mental health professional if indicated after further assessment
